sections.text: The Verge outlined its process for selecting Black Friday deals, noting that many promotional offers lack transparency. Research from Groundwork Collaborative indicates that a significant portion of Amazon deals do not provide actual savings, with some items costing more during sales events than in preceding weeks. Amazon disputes the methodology regarding how it calculates list prices.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Dynamic pricing and inflated discount claims make it difficult for shoppers to identify genuine bargains. Retailers often use list prices that do not reflect typical market rates, leading to consumer confusion. Consequently, publications like The Verge must perform independent vetting to ensure recommended products offer real value.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Verge will continue to curate a limited selection of deals based on product testing and historical price data. They intend to maintain transparency with readers by using independent tracking tools to verify discounts throughout the holiday shopping season.
